identity.method: Probe independently SHA-256-hashes the isolated file and the existing GUI view's entire Raw parent; checks the exact isolated database path, image base and architecture before each query. Original filename metadata still names the source DLSS file and does not override the verified database identity.

scope: Static read-only GUI Binary Ninja queries through bnctl. No game launch/attachment, CE, native calls, hooks, process writes, save access, driver/hypervisor, bypass, or BN name/type/comment changes. Existing GUI session is not saved, retargeted or closed. Only this JSON and the new probe are owned.

collection.method: Probe emits bounded JSON to stdout; caller preserves load-bearing raw instruction/HLIL excerpts here through explicit file tools. Excerpts are not claimed as whole-function listings unless specified. All addresses are static preferred VAs, not runtime addresses. Every function below inherits the identity SHA-256 above.
collection.permission_note: Initial combined inspection-and-filesystem-checkpoint script invocation was denied. Probe was reduced to read-only stdout output with no filesystem writes; that safer operation succeeded. No permission settings were changed.
collection.prototype_policy: Any BN-generated prototype is an analysis hypothesis. No native callable signature is verified by this artifact.
collection.reference_policy: BN database xrefs are bounded analysis evidence, not a proof of exhaustive reference coverage. Unsuccessful queries leave claims unknown.
collection.final_gui_status: Same PID 45336, same isolated bndb, IdleState, 295765 functions; not saved, closed or retargeted.

validation.probe_python_syntax: valid via ast.parse; final anchors preset also executed successfully in GUI BN
validation.method: Separate Python -I -B read-only validation of JSON/RVAs/evidence links; recomputed whole binary SHA-256; parsed PE section table and compared every recorded instruction byte sequence and numeric qword to raw file bytes. No script output files or pycache created.

evidence_gate: Static leads only; no runtime adapter or appearance/menu feature is ready or enabled. Call signatures, game-thread/context identity, canonical appearance state, ownership bounds, preview/commit semantics and safe refresh require independent validation.

claims.claim: Preserved uGUIEquipOuter registration and DTI accessor are revalidated in the exact binary. Registration passes the DTI address, name, parent-like address and 0x4cf0 to sub_14216ed60, then stores 0x142fa77c8 at the DTI's first qword. The accessor returns the DTI address.
0x142fa77c8 is the initialized DTI object's method table, distinct from the recovered GUI instance vtable.

DTI table +0x8 contains sub_140523680. That factory requests 0x4cf0 bytes with 0x10 alignment-like argument and tail-calls sub_140523950 on nonzero result. sub_140523950 calls sub_141fb3d10, stores 0x142fa77f8 at the object's first qword, and registers btnlist_tab and btngrdlink_list. The new table +0x20 contains the validated DTI accessor.

sub_140523950 is uGUIEquipOuter's instance constructor and 0x142fa77f8 its primary instance vtable; 0x4cf0 is its allocation size. This does not establish live object identity or any menu callback ABI.

Instance vtable +0x238 points to the ui/equip/equip_appearance resource getter, +0x250 to widget binding sub_1405256b0, +0x2d0 to enumeration sub_140525370, and +0x2d8 to a resetting helper sub_1405252f0. The pointer run ends before btnlist_tab text at +0x2e8.

Enumeration visits indices 0..0x2ef via sub_1416721d0. It retains only groups whose first nonzero native piece byte+0x13 is 2 or 3, applies other category/ID guards and availability-like predicates, deduplicates group+4 values, and appends uint32 IDs to GUI+0x2990+category*0xbc8 with a qword count at GUI+0x3550+category*0xbc8. IDs 0xc2/0xc3 take a five-part availability loop; the other branch passes part argument 6. These are catalog/menu bounds, not proven inventory bounds.

The shared availability-like predicate has a large ID switch and a fallback that maps ID via sub_1416b6e60 then tests a bit in context+0x102428. It is also consulted by row flags and activation paths.

The availability predicate is not established as current-ownership validation. Its bitset and special-case conditions must not be replaced with a global unlock bypass. Native record offsets are not established as the packed armor.am_dat schema.

Widget initialization stores GUI context at list+0x120 and callbacks at list+0x128=0x140524230, +0x130=0x140504e40, +0x210=0x140524970 and +0x138=0x140524a70. The activation-like +0x128 callback has direct one-part and five-part writes and dialog-bearing branches; it is not merely a renderer.

Activation synchronizes two different representations: the indexed-context accessor result+0xe7434 gets group+4, whereas the active-object getter result+0x13754 gets the native piece's uint16 at +0x1e. 0xffffffff clears fields. It then calls sub_142041700 with the player-like object, 1 and 0, followed by widget refreshes. A display accessor resolves context+0xe7434 through sub_141672160 and a part pointer at +0x18.

sub_142041700 is a native appearance/equipment refresh candidate, while sub_1405264a0 and sub_140526000 refresh list/current-equipment widgets. Observed call-site constants do not establish a safe API or accepted real-armor ID domain.

Activation dialog callable tables lead to sub_140523e60 (single-part replacement after five-field reset), sub_140524000 (five-part filtered application) and sub_140524170 -> sub_140523a50 (five-slot toggle/reset). The first two return before modifications unless *third_argument==0; the last handler returns unless its result argument is zero.

Those result==0 gates are confirmation-like semantics. Preview, cancel restoration, final persistence, event-code meanings and loadout integration remain unknown; the separate 0/1 event branches in sub_140524a70 enqueue other actions and must not be mislabeled as proven apply/cancel callbacks.
